candidate_relations.reason: Orbital compartment syndrome is a required component of the composite but omits Saturday night retinopathy.
Retinal detachment is present as serous fluid on exam/OCT, a manifestation rather than the compression-retinopathy syndrome.
Posterior scleritis is a different painful red-eye entity and does not explain NLP vision after prolonged intoxication and orbital tightness.
Wegener granulomatosis is a different orbital/retinal inflammatory disease without supporting systemic vasculitis data.
Compartment syndrome is the parent mechanical process but missing orbital localization and the retinopathy.
Cellulitis can mimic eyelid induration but does not account for NLP vision, high IOP, and angiographic nonperfusion after compression.
Churg-Strauss syndrome is a different systemic vasculitis not supported here.
Scleritis is not the ischemic compressive ocular process described.
NMOSD is a demyelinating optic-nerve disease, not orbital compression with retinal whitening.
Uveitis does not explain tense orbit, rhabdomyolysis, and choroidal/retinal filling delay.
Central retinal artery occlusion captures the macular whitening/arterial delay but omits orbital compression and the Saturday-night mechanism.
Optic neuropathy is a parent description of the RAPD/NLP vision missing orbital compression and retinopathy specificity.
Compressive optic neuropathy is part of orbital compression syndrome but omits Saturday night retinopathy.
Acute retinal necrosis is a necrotizing retinitis, not compressive ischemic retinopathy.
Rhabdomyolysis-induced Purtscher-like retinopathy is related ischemic retinopathy with incompatible mechanism relative to orbital compression after intoxication.
Orbital cellulitis is a different cause of a tight orbit and is not required by the intoxication-compression history.
Corneal edema/haze is a secondary anterior-segment finding from high IOP, not the syndrome.
Ocular ischemic syndrome is a related hypoperfusion picture missing the acute orbital compression/Saturday-night context.
Eales disease is a different peripheral retinal vasculitis and does not fit this acute NLP orbit.
Endophthalmitis is not supported by the compressive ischemic angiography pattern.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate; Saturday night retinopathy with orbital compression syndrome is not named as a composite
